purpose: Source identities and assertion disposition for safe Rust tokenizer loading/lifetime replay; retired C++ controls and opaque C ABI adapters are not compiled.

native_reader.boundary: Historical native-reader provenance only. Serving and replay now use the bounded safe Rust GGUF reader; no external reader or generated native holder remains.

retained_obligations.original: BPETokenizer is neither copy-constructible nor move-constructible.
retained_obligations.replacement: Rust Tokenizer owns its tables without Copy or Clone and borrowed byte/ID spans cannot escape their safe Rust lifetimes. The generated holder and raw pointer adapter are removed.

retained_obligations.original: Missing file does not create or publish an owner; success loads all token and merge indices including duplicates and releases GGUF metadata.
retained_obligations.replacement: Shared serving metadata intake and transactional safe owner replacement; metadata fixture observes exact token/merge read indices, and a real tiny GGUF confirms duplicate IDs and production required-special intake without weights.

retained_obligations.original: Failures at new, token insertion, merge insertion and finish release the candidate exactly once, preserve the old pointer, and release metadata.
retained_obligations.replacement: Test-only stage faults exercise the shared serving constructor. Real Tokenizer Drop counters verify exactly-once candidate cleanup, unchanged old-owner identity, metadata release and encoding recovery after construction/token/merge/finish/required-special failure.

retained_obligations.original: Missing tokens or merges, null token/merge strings and oversized counts fail without replacing the owner.
retained_obligations.replacement: Same-path typed metadata faults retain every missing token/merge, invalid string, oversized count and wrong array/element type case. Required special keys, scalar types and unsigned IDs outside i32 also reject without replacement.

retained_obligations.original: Special keys skip missing names, preserve [1,-1,1] signed conversion and request order; direct special spelling/ID and registration failures are surfaced.
retained_obligations.replacement: Historical optional-key request order and signed [1,-1,1] observations replay directly through add_special_id. Direct special registration and real empty/oversized failures remain covered. Serving separately preserves mandatory keys and strict unsigned-to-i32 admission.

retained_obligations.original: Encoding forwards embedded NUL text and EOS mode; empty results require no data; nonempty results are copied independently.
retained_obligations.replacement: The safe serving encoder observes a\0b through known IDs and both EOS modes. Results are owned Vec values; independent results survive tokenizer destruction and cannot represent inconsistent pointer/count pairs.

retained_obligations.original: Null result and null data errors clean up without leaking result storage.
retained_obligations.replacement: Safe Rust makes null handles, missing callbacks and inconsistent pointer/count owners unrepresentable. Encoding errors return before the safe copy closure; real result-owner Drop counters retain success/empty/copy-refusal/unwind cleanup, followed by successful reuse.

retained_obligations.original: Successful replacement frees the old owner, permits encoding recovery and balances final owners/results/GGUF contexts.
retained_obligations.replacement: Safe Option<Box<Tokenizer>> replacement publishes only a complete serving candidate and drops the displaced actual Tokenizer. Fixture metadata and real tiny GGUF controls retain unchanged old-owner identity on failure, successful replacement, recovery and final balances.

qualification_boundary: Safe Rust replacement controls replay immutable native observations and production metadata intake, with no live C ABI holder or native reader. Focused local checks leave hosted owning-crate build/link, actual pinned vocabulary captures, full-model speech quality, lifecycle, resource and distribution qualification pending.
